concepts.name: Database System
concepts.description: A coordinated collection of software and data that enables users to store, retrieve, and manage information efficiently.

concepts.name: Data Model
concepts.description: An abstract framework that defines how data is structured, stored, and related within a database.

concepts.name: Relational Model
concepts.description: A data model that represents information as tables (relations) with rows and columns, using keys to establish relationships.

concepts.name: SQL Language
concepts.description: A declarative language (including DDL and DML) used to define schemas, manipulate data, and query relational databases.

concepts.name: Schema and Instance
concepts.description: The schema is the structural definition of a database, while an instance is the actual data populating that structure at a given time.

concepts.name: Storage Manager
concepts.description: The component responsible for managing on‑disk storage, including file organization, indexing, and buffer management.

concepts.name: Query Processor
concepts.description: The subsystem that parses, optimizes, and executes SQL queries, translating them into low‑level operations on the storage manager.

concepts.name: Transaction Management
concepts.description: Mechanisms that ensure atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability (ACID) of concurrent database operations.

concepts.name: Relation
concepts.description: A relation is a set of tuples having the same attributes, representing a table in the relational model.

concepts.name: Attribute
concepts.description: An attribute is a named column of a relation that defines a data domain for its values.

concepts.name: Key
concepts.description: A key is a set of one or more attributes that uniquely identifies each tuple in a relation.

concepts.name: Relational Algebra
concepts.description: A formal language consisting of operators that manipulate relations to produce new relations.

concepts.name: Select Operation (σ)
concepts.description: Select extracts tuples from a relation that satisfy a given predicate.

concepts.name: Join Operation (⨝)
concepts.description: Join combines tuples from two relations based on a common attribute condition.

concepts.name: Schema Diagram
concepts.description: A visual representation of relations, their attributes, and key constraints within a database schema.

concepts.name: Aggregate Function
concepts.description: An aggregate computes a summary value (e.g., COUNT, SUM) over a set of tuples, often used with GROUP BY.

concepts.name: SQL Syntax
concepts.description: The basic textual structure and keywords used to write SQL statements.

concepts.name: CREATE TABLE
concepts.description: Statement that defines a new relation, its attributes, and their data types.

concepts.name: Integrity Constraints
concepts.description: Rules such as PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, and CHECK that enforce data validity.

concepts.name: SELECT Query Structure
concepts.description: The core query form consisting of SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, and ORDER BY clauses.

concepts.name: SQL Joins
concepts.description: Operations that combine rows from two or more tables using INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL, and CROSS joins.

concepts.name: Subqueries
concepts.description: Nested SELECT statements that can appear in SELECT, FROM, WHERE, or HAVING clauses.

concepts.name: Aggregate Functions & GROUP BY
concepts.description: Functions like COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX used with GROUP BY to summarize data.

concepts.name: WITH Clause (CTE)
concepts.description: Defines temporary named result sets (common table expressions) for use within a larger query.

concepts.name: Entity Set
concepts.description: A collection of similar entities that share the same attributes.

concepts.name: Relationship Set
concepts.description: A set of associations among entities, each instance linking specific entity occurrences.

concepts.name: Cardinality Constraints
concepts.description: Rules that specify the minimum and maximum number of entity instances that can participate in a relationship.

concepts.name: Weak Entity Set
concepts.description: An entity set that cannot be uniquely identified by its own attributes alone and depends on a owning (strong) entity.

concepts.name: Specialization / Generalization
concepts.description: A hierarchical modeling construct that groups entities into super‑type and sub‑type sets based on distinguishing attributes.

concepts.name: Aggregation
concepts.description: A modeling technique that treats a relationship set (and its participating entities) as a higher‑level entity for further relationships.

concepts.name: ER Diagram Notation
concepts.description: Standard symbols (rectangles, diamonds, ovals, etc.) used to visually represent entities, relationships, attributes, and constraints.

concepts.name: Mapping ER to Relational Schema
concepts.description: The systematic process of converting entity sets, relationship sets, and constraints into tables, columns, and keys in a relational database.

concepts.name: Functional Dependency
concepts.description: A constraint X → Y indicating that attribute set X uniquely determines attribute set Y in a relation.

concepts.name: Attribute Closure
concepts.description: The set of all attributes functionally implied by a given attribute set under a set of functional dependencies.

concepts.name: Lossless Decomposition
concepts.description: A decomposition of a relation into smaller relations that preserves the original information when the pieces are joined.

concepts.name: Dependency Preservation
concepts.description: A property of a decomposition where the union of functional dependencies of the component schemas is equivalent to the original set.

concepts.name: Third Normal Form (3NF)
concepts.description: A relation is in 3NF if for every non‑trivial functional dependency X → A, X is a superkey or A is a prime attribute.

concepts.name: Boyce‑Codd Normal Form (BCNF)
concepts.description: A stricter form of 3NF where for every non‑trivial functional dependency X → Y, X must be a superkey.

concepts.name: Multivalued Dependency (MVD)
concepts.description: A constraint X ↠ Y indicating that the set of Y values associated with X is independent of other attributes.

concepts.name: Fourth Normal Form (4NF)
concepts.description: A relation is in 4NF if it is in BCNF and has no non‑trivial multivalued dependencies other than a key.
